top_story_title: Check Point Security Management Server zero-day exploited since July; gateway pre-auth RCE under attack alongside it
top_story_summary: Check Point has released emergency Jumbo hotfixes for CVE-2026-93616, a pre-authentication path traversal in Security Management Server that lets an unauthenticated attacker reach the server's web service and upload and execute arbitrary scripts. Check Point Research says the flaw was exploited in a small number of targeted attacks as far back as July 23, 2026, and published the fix on September 22. CISA added it to the KEV catalog on September 22 with a remediation due date of September 25. Per the KEV entry, the same path traversal covers Multi-Domain Security Management Server, Log Server, Multi-Domain Log Server and SmartEvent.
top_actions: Apply the Check Point Jumbo hotfix for CVE-2026-93616 to Security Management Server, Multi-Domain Security Management Server, Log Server, Multi-Domain Log Server and SmartEvent now - the KEV due date is 2026-09-25.
Confirm every Security Gateway and Spark firewall carries the CVE-2026-85102 fix released on September 9; if the build predates it, treat the device as having been exposed to active exploitation.
Remove the management server's web service from any internet-reachable path and restrict it to a dedicated management VLAN or out-of-band network with an explicit source ACL.
Assume pre-patch compromise back to 2026-07-23: rotate management and gateway admin credentials, API keys, certificates and VPN pre-shared keys after the upgrade.
Export and diff the policy database and gateway configurations against a known-good backup, looking for unexpected admin users, rules, scripts or modified login pages.
executive_summary: Check Point patched CVE-2026-93616, a pre-auth script upload and execution flaw in Security Management Server exploited in targeted attacks since 2026-07-23; KEV due date 2026-09-25.
Check Point also confirms active exploitation of CVE-2026-85102, unauthenticated RCE on Security Gateway and Spark firewalls running Site-to-Site or Remote Access VPN; fix available since 2026-09-09.

F5 disclosed CVE-2026-94127 on 2026-09-22, a CVSS 9.8 heap overflow giving unauthenticated RCE on BIG-IP APM - only where a virtual server has both an APM access policy and an OAuth profile. Engineering hotfixes released; exploited as a zero-day, now in KEV.

Arista reported active exploitation of CVE-2026-93952 in on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator (CVSS 10.0), affecting only orchestrators that authenticate Edges with certificates. In KEV, due 2026-09-25.
D-Link disclosed a maximum-severity flaw in legacy DIR-822A Wi-Fi routers, CVE-2026-86296, with public PoC code and no patch - replacement or isolation is the only answer.
A Chinese-speaking threat actor exploited Zyxel GS1900 smart managed switches, reaching 996 devices and more than 18,500 records in backend databases.
Three of the four exploited flaws this cycle hit management and orchestration platforms rather than data-plane devices; prioritise the controllers before the edge.
key_actions: **Multiple** — Patch the Check Point Security Management Server first, then gateways; then the BIG-IP APM units - management and access control planes before data plane.
**Multiple** — Verify each Check Point gateway is on the 2026-09-09 or later build that fixes CVE-2026-85102; anything older has been exposed to probing for two weeks.
**F5** — Apply F5's engineering hotfix to all units in the device group and verify config sync after upgrade; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release that applies to your branch.
**F5** — Inventory virtual servers for the exposed combination - an APM access policy together with an OAuth profile - and prioritise those; other configurations are not affected.
**Arista** — Patch the on-premises orchestrator before touching Edge devices, and validate certificate trust after the upgrade; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release.
**Arista** — Determine whether your VCO authenticates Edges with certificates - that is the exposed configuration per Arista.
**F5** — Enumerate virtual servers and filter for the pairing of an APM access policy with an OAuth profile; that list is your patch queue.
**F5** — Apply the F5 hotfix across the device group and verify config sync; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release for your branch.

ai_defenses.what_it_does: Check Point describes this as the program under which it continues to release Jumbo hotfixes carrying security fixes and hardening improvements for its Firewall and Management products. The advisory gives no further detail on the program's scope.

headlines.title: Attackers hit Check Point Management Servers and Spark firewalls, F5 BIG-IP APM instances
headlines.summary: Check Point and F5 are both responding to in-the-wild exploitation: two Check Point CVEs added to KEV, plus an unauthenticated RCE zero-day in F5 BIG-IP APM.

headlines.title: F5 Patches Critical BIG-IP APM Zero-Day Exploited for Unauthenticated RCE on OAuth Servers
headlines.summary: F5 says attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-94127 in BIG-IP APM to run code without logging in, on systems where APM acts as an OAuth authorization server.

headlines.title: New CVSS 10.0 VeloCloud Orchestrator Flaw Actively Exploited in Certificate-Based Setups
headlines.summary: Arista reports active exploitation of CVE-2026-93952, a CVSS 10.0 input validation flaw in on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator, in certificate-authenticated deployments.

headlines.title: CVE-2026-94127: Critical Unauthenticated RCE in F5 BIG-IP APM
headlines.summary: Rapid7 details CVE-2026-94127 as a CVSS 9.8 heap-based buffer overflow in BIG-IP APM, reachable only when a virtual server has both an access policy and an OAuth profile.

headlines.title: Check Point Warns of Management Server Zero-Day Exploited in Targeted Attacks
headlines.summary: Check Point's Security Management Server carried a zero-day, CVE-2026-93616, letting unauthenticated attackers run scripts on the server that controls firewall policy.

headlines.title: Security Advisory – Action Required – Active Exploitation of CVE-2026-85102 and a Management Pre-Authentication Vulnerability CVE-2026-93616
headlines.summary: Check Point's own advisory confirms active exploitation of two flaws: CVE-2026-85102 on Security Gateway and the new pre-auth CVE-2026-93616 in Security Management.
